market_view: Thursday was a broad AI selloff, not a demand scare: the Nasdaq fell 2.6% (worst since June 5) and the chip index 6.7% after Meta posted its first negative free cash flow in over a decade and said it will issue new non-voting shares to fund AI spending, and Lam Research cited supply-chain limits (Reuters, AP, Oct 22), while index futures were roughly flat around 8:45 PM ET. Tonight's after-hours earnings movers (RingCentral +15%, Robert Half +10%) are already priced in, and with stops forced under Thursday's close they can't offer 1.5:1, so I add no new trades and only manage my five compounders.
lessons: The playbook's evidence table says I am losing to the market: alpha -2.28% per trade over 22 closed trades (95% range -4.11% to -0.45%) with only a 1.8% chance of beating the Fruit Fly (-0.38% average), and I trail Momentum too (-1.58%); my moonshot book is 1 win in 10 at -3.61% (a hunch at n=10, but all bad), so I again submit zero moonshots instead of guessing on Friday's pre-open prints like AXP and SLB.

INTU paid off because I cut its target from 360 to 345 near its recent intraday highs on Oct 18: it hit 345 for about +3.6%, while the original 360 would have missed by two dollars (the high was 358.03), which matches Claude's CRM and TMUS fades; I will keep setting swing targets at recent highs rather than round numbers above them.

Four of my five compounders are the same AI-capex bet and fell together as the chip index lost 6.7% (NVDA -4.4%, TSM -4.5%, GOOGL -3.2%, MSFT -2.1%), the same concentration Claude blamed for its NVDA stop at -11.6% (rated high) and fixed by adding LLY, which then hit its target for +11.25%; when a compounder slot frees I will fill it with a non-AI business, and I won't widen stops on losing positions to dodge the hit.
